description: The reviewed rule pack for observations_agree(run, check, scenario_set, policy) and incumbent_stable(run) (Lane A). observations_agree says only that, on the scenarios the admitted set declares, the incumbent and the candidate were observed to answer alike under the admitted comparison policy -- it is NOT a correctness claim and not a capability-parity claim. NO MODEL RELATION IS DECLARED: neither this pack nor schema_observation_v1.json declares a model relation or a model producer class, so the claim is model-free BY CONSTRUCTION; and model_conformance_unassessed is a POSITIVE, CLOSED premise, so the claim does not derive unless the receipt states in exported rows that it assessed no model. A receipt that carries a model belongs to op_qualified in the replay pack, not here. There is NO experiments/claim-semantics mirror of this pack in v1 -- there is no corpus adapter for observation receipts yet, so this shipped file is the only copy and nobody should look for a second one. Every relation is runtime-bound, so no static/runtime compatibility witness is needed or declared (a compatibility relation here would be ceremony a later reader would mistake for a gate). The receipt's source binding is a context-free reviewer observation joined on a column of the run row, exactly as replay_run_current binds a snapshot. C4 (one-sided masks): observation_body_raw is read by body_masked, which holds where a scenario's two raw body digests differ while its two normalized body digests match -- a real wire difference that a normalization erased, on one side or on both. observation_mask_undisclosed holds where such a scenario has no observation_masked_difference row for the body facet, and observations_agree negates it under observation_mask_disclosure_closed. This is the judge's own copy of the exporter's R-9: an erased difference that reached the bundle undisclosed blocks the claim here even if it was not refused at ingest.
